newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn CDU blames SPD for not resuming tax talks.
newsitem.headline: Bonn CDU blames SPD for not resuming tax talks.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) on Friday blamed the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) for the failure to resume talks on tax reform, the next step to getting the economy back on track.
CDU general secretary Peter Hintze called SPD head Oskar Lafontaine's demand for a personal meeting with Kohl a "transparent diversionary manoeuvre".

After a first high-level meeting between Kohl and Lafontaine last month, another meeting was held by a working group to discuss technical issues of the tax reform. It was the SPD that called off the second working group meeting to protest against the government's plan to curtail coal subsidies.
"The coal problem has been solved. There is no further objective obstacle to a working group meeting," Hintze said.
"If the SPD continues to boycott the tax working group, it must take the full responsibility for the delay of tax reform, Hintze said. Kohl has no reason to meet with Lafontaine personally, he added.

Kohl has sought the SPD talks to ease the passage of Finance Minister Theo Waigel's package of tax reform measures through parliament. The SPD's majority in the upper house gives it the power to block at least part of the proposals.
The package includes a net 30 billion marks in tax cuts aimed at stimulating investment and jobs creation.
